note: Reviewed CDB90 match 65, pinned revision e0b35ec4d798cec3bb4e6970c0f6bb7aa69e2f4c. CDB90 (CAA Database of Battles, Version 1990), tidy data maintained by Jeffrey B. Arnold. Original US Army Concepts Analysis Agency data; revised data licensed ODC-BY. Original force designations and strength interpretations are retained with each quantity. Each side is one aggregate force, including any coalition; its total is not allocated among members. Personnel casualties are not deaths. Source estimates and adjudged error margins are not statistical confidence intervals. Equipment and tactical movements are not established by this dataset. Match review: Approved whole-battle match for the land engagement near Prague on 6 May 1757, also called Štěrboholy. The explicit articleAliasReview binds the CDB title to public Q223622; NAM distinguishes this field battle from the subsequent siege, and the RCT map names Frederick II’s Prussian army and Charles of Lorraine’s Austrian army. Retain the two complete source force rows as single local military aggregates: PR ARMY 65000 and AUS ARMY 62000, both code 1 initial personnel, with zero tabulated reinforcements. Personnel battle casualties are 14300 and 13400, not deaths. These remain attributed CDB90 estimates with its raw uncertainty qualifiers; the institutional evidence establishes identity and scope, not independent numerical certification. No siege losses, relief army, additional constituent armies or equipment assignments are added. Article alias review (2026-09-22; Q223622; Battle_of_Prague_(1757) -> Battle_of_Štěrboholy): The source URL was opened directly and displayed an explicit redirect from Battle of Prague (1757) to Battle of Štěrboholy, with its Wikidata link pointing to Q223622. The cached HTML and target revision preserve this identity check. Institutional sources independently identify the same dated engagement. This is a reviewed spelling/title equivalence, not a fuzzy match or permission to broaden the source force cohort. Identity review (attacker; original CDB90 name PR ARMY): Local battle-force identity for the source PR ARMY under FREDERICK II. The RCT map names this command at the 6 May field battle. This is one aggregate, not an additional army or the later siege force. Identity review (defender; original CDB90 name AUS ARMY): Local battle-force identity for the source AUS ARMY under LORRAINE. The RCT map names this command at the 6 May field battle. It does not include a separately invented relief force or add troops from the later siege.
